findings.title: Reject dangling output symlinks before resolving them
findings.message: Resolving the output before checking its existence follows an existing dangling symlink. If its target is a nonexistent .app path, validation passes and the bundle is published at the symlink target rather than rejecting the existing output path.
findings.suggestion: Resolve only the output's parent directory and reject both existing paths and dangling symlinks before packaging.

findings.title: Prevent the manifest from overwriting input artifacts
findings.message: The manifest destination is only checked against the bundle directory. Supplying the binary or library path as --manifest therefore succeeds and replaces that input artifact with JSON, destroying the previously built executable or dylib. Resolving the manifest path also makes this possible through a symlink to an input.
findings.suggestion: Reject manifest destinations that resolve to either input artifact before doing any packaging work. Consider requiring a new manifest path as well if overwriting existing manifests is not intended.

fix.before: if args.manifest.resolve().is_relative_to(output):raise ValueError('manifest must be outside the sealed bundle')
fix.after:
if args.manifest.resolve().is_relative_to(output):raise ValueError('manifest must be outside the sealed bundle')
 if args.manifest.resolve() in (binary,library):raise ValueError('manifest must not overwrite an input artifact')
